target.title: fix(sessions): prune stale entries independently of maxEntries gate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issue #103956: the `session.pruneAfter` configuration setting is silently ignored during normal gateway operation. Sessions older than the configured prune cutoff grow unbounded regardless of the `pruneAfter` duration.

## Why This Change Was Made

During load-time session store maintenance, stale-entry pruning (`pruneStaleEntries`) was gated by `Object.keys(store).length > maintenance.maxEntries`. This meant age-based pruning only fired when the store exceeded its entry count limit. If a user had fewer sessions than `maxEntries` (default 500), no pruning ever happened ??`pruneAfter` effectively became dead configuration.

The fix separates the pruning trigger from the entry-count gate, matching the established pattern in `applyEnforcedMaintenance()` in `store-maintenance-operations.ts` which already runs `pruneStaleEntries` unconditionally in enforce mode.

## User Impact

Users who configure `session.maintenance.pruneAfter` will now see sessions older than the configured duration automatically removed during load-time maintenance, regardless of how many sessions exist. The entry-count cap (`maxEntries`) continues to work exactly as before ??it is still gated by `shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance`.

## Evidence

**Root cause**: In `src/config/sessions/store-load.ts`, the `pruneStaleEntries` call at load-time was inside an `if` condition `maintenance.mode === "enforce" && Object.keys(store).length > maintenance.maxEntries`. Removing the entry-count gate restores independent age-based pruning.

The fix is a structural mirror of `applyEnforcedMaintenance()` in `store-maintenance-operations.ts`, which already runs `pruneStaleEntries` unconditionally (when mode is `"enforce"`):

```typescript
// store-maintenance-operations.ts (correct behavior ??runs pruning unconditionally)
const pruned = pruneStaleEntries(store, maintenance.pruneAfterMs, { ... });
const countAfterPrune = Object.keys(store).length;
const shouldRunCapMaintenance = shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance({ ... });
```

```typescript
// store-load.ts (after fix ??same pattern)
pruned = pruneStaleEntries(store, maintenance.pruneAfterMs, { ... });
const countAfterPrune = Object.keys(store).length;
capped = shouldRunSessionEntryMaintenance({ ... }) ? capEntryCount(...) : 0;
```

Diff: only `src/config/sessions/store-load.ts` ??3 lines changed, 1 removed.

Evidence tier: L2 (vitest + fixture)
Proof limitations: Unit-level verification covers pruning logic and the load-time path.

## Tests

```powershell
npx vitest run src/config/sessions/store.pruning.test.ts --no-coverage --reporter=basic
npx vitest run src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts --no-coverage --reporter=basic
pnpm check:changed
pnpm format:check
```

## Risk

- Behavior change: Yes ??stale pruning now works as documented
- Config change: No
- Data loss risk: Low ??pruning uses the same `pruneAfterMs` threshold already configured; no new deletion path
- Performance impact: Low ??`pruneStaleEntries` is O(n) on session count and was already called during every load-time maintenance pass when over the entry limit

## Current Review State

Ready for review.

---

target.title: fix(minimax): add timeouts to OAuth HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MiniMax OAuth login could wait indefinitely when either the device-code request or token-poll request accepted the HTTP connection but never returned a response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OAuth flow already bounds polling and authorization expiry, but each outbound HTTP request lacked its own deadline. This change gives both guarded POSTs one provider-owned 30-second deadline while preserving PKCE payloads, SSRF hostname policy, bounded error reads, and polling behavior.

Maintainer preparation kept that timeout internal instead of exposing a test-only override. The regressions capture the production timeout callback and fire it only after a real loopback server confirms request receipt, so they prove stalled-response behavior without short wall-clock races.

## User Impact

A stalled MiniMax OAuth endpoint no longer leaves login wedged. Authorization-code and token-poll hangs reject boundedly instead of waiting forever.

## Evidence

- Exact prepared head: `0eebecc63a6a98552e0224c95097e6c8251aa8b5`.
- Sanitized public-network AWS Crabbox `run_f4ac0dda4e25`: `pnpm test extensions/minimax/oauth.test.ts` passed, 1 file and 14 tests.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx7n3r5489aa45a154b1hrkd`, Actions run 29138804960: deterministic timeout fix passed the same 14 tests.
- Fresh autoreview after the test fix: no accepted or actionable findings; patch correct at 0.98 confidence.
- Exact-head hosted CI run 29138962126: scoped lint, types, security, dependency, build, and test checks passed; its two QA Smoke failures match the active release baseline on `main`.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests use a real `node:http` loopback server that accepts requests and deliberately never responds. A bare fetch is first confirmed received and still pending without a deadline. The exported `loginMiniMaxPortalOAuth` path is then exercised for both authorization-code and token-poll requests; after the server confirms receipt, the captured production 30-second deadline is fired and each request rejects with abort/timeout semantics.

Live MiniMax account approval was not exercised. The exact network failure mode is reproduced locally without third-party credentials.

target.title: fix(codex): prefer the pinned runtime for current models
target.body:
Closes #103884

## What Problem This Solves

Users selecting a newly supported Codex model could still get a “requires a newer version” failure when an older macOS desktop bundle shadowed the current Codex app-server packaged with OpenClaw. Switching between the pinned runtime and native Computer Use state also needed an exact, race-safe handoff so a thread could not load config under one executable owner and continue under another.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary managed Codex turns now prefer the pinned `@openai/codex` package. User-home and effective Computer Use configurations stay desktop-first because their native state and macOS permissions belong to that desktop runtime, with the pinned package retained as fallback when no desktop binary is available.

The handoff is bound to the exact spawned process identity and serialized inside one Gateway across native config-loading thread requests and Computer Use installation. Selection drift retires the old physical client and performs a bounded, replay-safe retry only when the request was proven not to have been written. Post-write cancellation or transport failure keeps the config fence through physical process exit and is never classified replay-safe.

Legacy one-off Computer Use identity flags now return literal-safe migration guidance for persistent `computerUse.pluginName` / `computerUse.mcpServerName` configuration. Explicit app-server command overrides remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Current Codex models use the OpenClaw-pinned runtime by default even when an older desktop app is installed. Computer Use continues to run under the desktop app that owns its local permissions and persisted native state. CLI status/install guidance preserves custom identities and marketplace arguments exactly.

The native-config fence coordinates one running Gateway process. After another Codex process or Gateway changes native plugin config, restart the Gateway and start a new chat before relying on the new selection.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx7j9nwct0kgxr6nynkzjafp`: 516 focused Codex extension tests passed, plus 17 embedded-runner app-server recovery tests.
- Blacksmith Testbox: `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed on the final snapshot.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Structured Codex autoreview and a separate focused lifecycle review reported no accepted/actionable P1 or compile findings after the final replay-safety fix.
- Upstream Codex source was inspected for initialize identity, native config loading on thread start/resume/fork, plugin-install persistence, npm launcher/platform-package selection, and app-server CLI config semantics. The fix selects and tracks the real executable rather than spoofing `clientInfo.version`.

AI-assisted change; implementation and validation were reviewed by the maintainer agent.
